frontmatter.title: Thermal spectral filtering with retargeted QSP
frontmatter.description: Generated even/odd phases, explicit Hamiltonian access and Bell preparation, with bounded thermal checks and logical-source error contracts.

children.value: A spectral filter can suppress high-energy amplitudes without expanding powers of the Hamiltonian into a Pauli-word table. This method applies an exponential-shaped QSP polynomial through the original Hamiltonian’s access circuit. It advances the
to newly generated phases for each Hamiltonian size and inverse temperature. The coefficients used for fitting are classical scalar data; no eigenvectors or matrix exponential are loaded into a gate.

Actual phase generation, PREPARE/SELECT/unprepare access, a real parity selector, Bell preparation and complete measured trials are implemented. The generator supplies bounded gate/reference checks and separate larger circuit-only counts. Analytic/interval bounds cover the declared logical circuit with exact controls and stored binary64 rotation angles. The complete-resource study below supplies actual Clifford+T trials and a separate conditional instrument model for one and two spins. SDK realization and synthesis checks remain numerical; general thermal mixing, hardware validation and formal/Lean proofs remain planned.

The nine displayed cases are checked on the actual source circuits. The accepted filter block is extracted from the provided circuit by inverse-Bell preparation and data-basis Statevector trajectories, within an effective system-plus-success width of eight and a full Bell-statevector width of twelve. This is a bounded filter-operator check, not a full larger-wire unitary check. For larger Bell-plus-filter circuits, compilation equivalence is checked only on the all-zero input state; it is not a full-unitary certificate. All results use ideal CPU simulation, without executed quantum shots or physical noise.

T/T-dagger operations also charge capped complete factory retries, neighboring SWAP transport, injection/readout/correction, port recycling and extra handoff residence. Native output-quality faults and factory readiness are separate model contributions.

Two-spin energy uses one common distance and one common factory size, pipeline time and output error across its groups. Only candidates feasible for both X and Z are combined: elapsed times and allocated failure contributions add, while sequential peak qubits take the maximum. The per-group factory retry caps remain charged. Selecting incompatible per-group qubit/time minima would not define the reported shared-hardware workload.

energy_rows=[]
for scenario,report in results["energy"].items():
    points=report["pareto_points"]
    point=min(points,key=lambda p:(p["peak_physical_qubits"],p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"])) if points else None
    if point:
        groups=point["group_points"]
        common=lambda p:(p["data_code_distance"],p["reserved_logical_patches"],p["factory_physical_qubits"],p["factory_supply"]["pipeline_time_ns"],p["factory_supply"]["output_error"])
        assert common(groups["X"])==common(groups["Z"])
        assert point["peak_physical_qubits"]==max(p["peak_physical_qubits"] for p in groups.values())
        assert point["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]==sum(p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"] for p in groups.values())
    energy_rows.append({"scenario":scenario,"status":report["status"],
        "common_candidates":report["common_feasible_candidate_count"],
        "peak_qubits":point["peak_physical_qubits"] if point else None,
        "runtime_hours":point["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]/3.6e12 if point else None})
table(pd.DataFrame(energy_rows))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.8))
feasible=[r for r in energy_rows if r["peak_qubits"] is not None]
for i,row in enumerate(feasible):
    ax.scatter(row["peak_qubits"],row["runtime_hours"],s=65,marker="o" if "controller1e-15" in row["scenario"] else "^",color=("#365e88" if "p1e-03" in row["scenario"] else "#a56737"),label=row["scenario"])
if feasible:
    ax.set(xscale="log",yscale="log",xlim=(min(r["peak_qubits"] for r in feasible)*.8,max(r["peak_qubits"] for r in feasible)*1.2),ylim=(min(r["runtime_hours"] for r in feasible)*.9,max(r["runtime_hours"] for r in feasible)*1.1))
    ax.legend(loc="upper left",fontsize=8)
else:
    ax.text(.5,.5,"No common feasible energy configuration in the declared model",ha="center",va="center",transform=ax.transAxes)
ax.set(xlabel="Peak physical qubits at a shared configuration",ylabel="All-attempt runtime (hours)",title="Calculated two-spin energy; hardware execution unperformed")
ax.grid(alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
